reason: Before the PR, REGEX_FORMAT matched Y{1,4} but format() only implemented YY and YYYY, so a lone 'Y' and 'YYY' fell through to the timezone-offset fallback and rendered as '+0000'-style offsets instead of literal 'Y'/'24Y'.

After the PR, REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY and YY, so a lone 'Y' is left unmatched and preserved literally, while 'YYY' consumes the leading 'YY' as a two-digit year and leaves the trailing 'Y' as a literal, yielding '24Y'.
The PR is a behavior-preserving refactor that extracts the existing decode-if-has-percent check; at base the route-parameter decode path already decoded %20 to a space before reading.
The refactored tryDecodeURIComponent utility performs the same 'contains %' check then percent-decodes, so the route parameter is still decoded to a literal space.

The PR description explicitly states that reschedule wrote the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updated @score, so reading score/at off the same entry handle returned the stale pre-reschedule time.
The fix adds @score = at.to_f after zincrby, so the in-memory SortedEntry handle immediately reports the newly requested reschedule time.
The PR only changes Range header parsing (parseRangesSpecifier); Content-Type parsing is untouched, so 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' still yields type text/plain with charset UTF-8.
The whitespace-trimming fix is confined to Range parsing and does not affect Content-Type parsing, which still reports text/plain with charset UTF-8.
The PR only alters warning/exception message strings in ComposerRepository; zip archiving timestamp behavior is unrelated and already preserves source file mtimes.
The message-logging change does not touch the archive command, so both extractions still preserve source modification times and show no 1980-01-01 dates.
The PR changes only CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix prefix matching; async JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsync of a list with a nullable parent property is unrelated and deserializes without error.
The case-sensitive path comparison change is unrelated to System.Text.Json, so synchronous and asynchronous deserialization of the same payload still both succeed and agree.
The PR fixes FETCH FIRST on empty WITH HOLD cursors in sql_cursor.go; the INET <<= ANY comparison path is untouched and already parses and returns true.
The cursor fix does not touch INET operators, so the >>= ANY array comparison still parses and returns true without a syntax error.
Before the PR every NO_PROXY entry was wildcard-prefixed into 'all://*::1', which the later URLPattern parsing could not interpret, causing client construction to raise an error.
After the PR an IPv6 hostname is detected and mounted as 'all://[::1]', so the client constructs without error and recognizes ::1 as a no-proxy host.
Before the fix, Series.str.match rejected regex flags other than re.IGNORECASE (included DOTALL), so requesting the dot-matches-newline option raised instead of returning matches.
The fix restores non-IGNORECASE flags, so DOTALL is honored both via flags and via a pre-compiled re.Pattern, making 'a\nc' match 'a.c' while 'ac' does not.

The chain with a group in the middle and more tasks after it hits the bug the PR fixes; at base the wrong prev_task/prev_res parents are recorded during freeze, so the serialized/reconstructed result tree does not preserve all four group children.
The fix re-sets prev_task/prev_res after each sequential group, so the reconstructed result tree correctly keeps a separate child result for every task in both groups.
Without the fix, encountering '--' switches the parser into trailing-values mode instead of consuming it as the current positional's terminator, so the first positional captures '--check' as well.
The fix makes the current positional's value_terminator take precedence over trailing-values mode, so the first positional stops at '--' and the second positional collects '--check' as expected.

At base the OSC11 handler calls nvim_set_option_value('background', ...) which, arriving after VimEnter, triggers the registered OptionSet 'background' autocommand and the ColorScheme autocommand as the test expects.

The fix wraps the background set in ':noautocmd', explicitly suppressing the OptionSet event on late-arriving OSC11 responses, so the OptionSet (and ColorScheme) autocommands the test expects to fire no longer fire.
The PR only reorders compile-time @derive reads in Ecto.Schema; changeset cast/required validation is runtime behavior and is unaffected, still flagging the omitted field as blank and invalid.
The compile-time derive reordering does not change runtime cast/validate behavior, so an omitted required field still yields an invalid changeset with a 'can't be blank' error.
